blocks.html:
The Laboratory of Modern Languages offers English language courses from level B1 to level C1 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR).
Each course aims to develop comprehension and production skills, both oral and written.

English language courses open to USI community free of charge

Language courses open to USI Alumni and students from other Swiss universities fee-based

Language courses open to external users fee-based

items.title: Why study English?
items.html:
• An excellent knowledge of English broadens study and career opportunities in Switzerland and abroad;
  • An international recognised certification is a requirement for admission to most universities;
  • In Switzerland, a high level of proficiency in at least two of the country’s official languages is generally required, together with an excellent knowledge of English;
  • The Laboratory of Modern Languages offers free language courses to all USI members in order to promote language learning and foster multilingualism within the academic community;
  • For students enrolled in the Bachelor’s programmes in Communication and Economics, achieving a B2+ level of English proficiency constitutes a formative requirement;
  • An excellent knowledge of English is essential for successfully completing a Master's degree programme and a PhD;
  • A high level of proficiency is often a requirement for USI's Exchange programmes;
  • For Bachelor’s students in Communication, the C1 English language course allow students to obtain ECTS credits within the Skills area;
  • English is the lingua franca of science and research.

items.title: English language proficiency certifications
items.html: To graduate with a Bachelor’s degree from the Faculty of Communication, Culture and Society or the Faculty of Economics, students are required to demonstrate a specific level of English proficiency. For further information, please visit the following page. The same page also provides information on the language certifications accepted for admission to Master’s degree programmes.
